questions.q: What is true about the colour and shape of a sign in Israel?
options: The background colour on a guide sign says nothing about the type of destination
A triangle with a red border is always a warning sign
All the signs in series 300 share exactly the same shape
A blue circle is always a prohibition sign
questions.explain: A triangle with the point up and a red border always identifies a warning sign (series 100). In series 300 every sign has a deliberately different shape, and a blue circle is a mandatory sign, not a prohibition sign.

questions.q: The traffic light shows red, but a police officer is standing at the junction signalling “go” with their hand. What must you do?
options: Choose whichever is more convenient at that moment
Go, because a police officer's instruction overrides the traffic light
Stop, because a red light always overrides a person's instruction
Wait for the green light and ignore the police officer
questions.explain: A road user must obey a police officer's instruction even when it contradicts a traffic light or a sign (reg. 23).

questions.q: What is the role of a supplementary sign, such as one placed under another sign and carrying a number in metres?
options: To serve only as decoration, with no legal meaning
To add information to the sign above it, such as a distance or a section of road
To replace the sign above it completely
To cancel the validity of the sign above it
questions.explain: A supplementary sign is not an independent sign; it adds information to the sign above it - for example a distance, a section of road, a direction or an exception.

questions.q: On a section of road a permanent speed sign shows 80, and next to it a temporary orange worksite sign shows 40. Which speed applies?
options: You may choose, because both signs are valid together
40, because the temporary worksite sign overrides the permanent one
80, because that is the permanent sign
60, the average of the two signs
questions.explain: A temporary worksite sign overrides the permanent sign at the same place, for as long as the work continues.

questions.q: What does the sign mean?
options: A side road merging from the right
The road narrows from the right
Falling rocks from the right
Sharp bend to the right
questions.explain: Sign 102 warns of a sharp bend to the right.

questions.q: According to the sign, when does the turn actually happen?
options: 300 metres from the sign
Only after the sign
Only if there is a traffic light at the junction
Before the sign itself
questions.explain: In a warning and guidance sign for a sharp bend, like sign 108, the turn happens before the board, not after it.

questions.q: The road you are driving on merges into a priority road coming from the right. What must you do?
options: Accelerate and go first
Make a full stop in every case
Turn right onto the side road
Give way to traffic on the road you are merging into
questions.explain: Sign 125 warns that your road merges into a priority road from the right - you must give way, and there is no turn onto a side road.

questions.q: What does the sign mean?
options: Pedestrians, usually children, nearby
Cyclists nearby
Educational-institutions area
Pedestrian crossing nearby
questions.explain: Sign 136 warns of pedestrians, usually children, nearby - for example near a school.

questions.q: What does the sign mean?
options: Railway crossing - a single track only
Railway crossing about 300 metres ahead
Railway crossing about 200 metres ahead
Railway crossing about 100 metres ahead
questions.explain: The countdown signs are 130 (about 300 metres), 131 (about 200 metres) and 132 (about 100 metres) before the crossing, unless a different distance is stated.

questions.q: A driver sees a sign warning of deep standing water on the road ahead, after heavy rain. What should they do?
options: Drive in fast, to avoid getting stuck in the water
Not enter the flooded section, and look for an alternative route
Enter slowly in a high gear
Enter only if another vehicle has already gone through
questions.explain: Sign 153 warns of deep standing water - don't drive into a flooded area; flowing or deep water can sweep a vehicle away or stall it.

questions.q: What does the sign require?
options: Turn right or left
Continue straight ahead only; a U-turn is forbidden
Turn right only
Choose between straight ahead and left
questions.explain: Sign 203 requires continuing straight ahead only (or in the direction of the diagonal arrow if shown); a U-turn is forbidden.

questions.q: What does a minimum speed sign require?
options: Slow down for the next junction
Not to exceed the speed shown on the sign
To drive at least at the speed shown on the sign
To avoid entering the expressway
questions.explain: A minimum speed sign (218) is for vehicles that can and are permitted to travel at least at the speed shown on it.

questions.q: What is true about driving in a shared street?
options: The street is for vehicles only
Entry by any private vehicle is completely forbidden
Pedestrians and children share the road with vehicles, and you must drive very slowly and give way to them
The driving speed there is the same as on an ordinary urban road
questions.explain: In a shared street, pedestrians, children playing and vehicles share the same road; you must drive very slowly and give way to pedestrians.

questions.q: What does the sign indicate?
options: A one-way lane for cyclists only
Entry is forbidden for bicycles
Start of a expressway
A path shared by pedestrians and cyclists
questions.explain: Sign 224 marks a one-way lane for bicycles, including electric bicycles; you ride in it only in the direction shown.

questions.q: What applies from the moment you enter a expressway?
options: Special driving rules, and entry is forbidden to pedestrians, cyclists and slow vehicles
Entry is permitted for every road user, including pedestrians
The maximum speed drops compared with the road before the sign
There is no change in the rules compared with an ordinary urban road
questions.explain: From the moment you enter a expressway, special rules apply; entry is forbidden to pedestrians, cyclists, animals and any vehicle that cannot or is not permitted to travel at least 60 km/h (sign 216).

questions.q: What does the sign require?
options: Turn right only
Slowing down and giving way to traffic on the crossing road; stopping only if necessary
A full stop in every case
Accelerating to cross the junction before the oncoming traffic
questions.explain: Sign 301 (give way) requires you to slow down and give way; a stop is required only if the situation demands it, not in every case.

questions.q: A vehicle reaches a junction with a stop sign. The crossing road looks completely empty. What must the driver do?
options: Sound the horn and continue without stopping
Stop only if a vehicle is seen approaching
Make a full stop before the stop line, and only then continue
Slow down slightly and continue without stopping, because the road is empty
questions.explain: Sign 302 requires a full stop, even when the road looks completely clear - the duty doesn't depend on what you can see.

questions.q: How do you enter and drive in a roundabout?
options: You drive in whichever direction you choose
You go around keeping to the right, anticlockwise, and give way to anyone already in the roundabout
You go around keeping to the left, clockwise
You make a full stop at the entrance in every case
questions.explain: When entering a roundabout you give way to a vehicle already in it, and go around keeping to the right, anticlockwise.

questions.q: You are driving on a road marked with sign 309. Until when does your priority apply at junctions?
options: Until the next junction or interchange, or until sign 310
Only at the first junction
Forever, until the end of the road
Until the local authority's boundary
questions.explain: The priority granted by sign 309 applies until the next junction or interchange, or until sign 310 marks its end.

questions.q: On a narrow section of road, a sign requires you to give way to traffic from the opposite direction. What does it mean?
options: Both directions must stop together
The vehicle facing you must wait for you
You must wait and let the oncoming vehicle pass first
The narrow section is closed to two-way traffic
questions.explain: Sign 307 requires you to give way to a vehicle coming from the opposite direction on the narrow section; the matching sign, which sets the opposite, is sign 308.

questions.q: What does the sign forbid?
options: Overtaking a motor vehicle with two wheels or more, until the next junction or the end sign
Any entry by a vehicle to the section of road
Parking on the side of the road
Driving with a maximum permitted weight over 4 tonnes
questions.explain: Sign 420 forbids overtaking a motor vehicle with two wheels or more, until the next junction or sign 421.

questions.q: What is the difference between sign 432 and sign 433?
options: There is no difference between them
432 also forbids a short stop; 433 permits it
432 applies only at night; 433 applies only during the day
432 forbids parking only and permits a short stop; 433 also forbids stopping
questions.explain: Sign 432 forbids parking only, and a short stop, loading or unloading, and picking up passengers are still permitted. Sign 433 forbids all stopping and parking.

questions.q: What does the sign forbid when it's placed above the traffic light at a junction?
options: Entering the junction in any direction
Turning right at the next junction only
Turning left only
Turning right, including a U-turn to the right
questions.explain: Sign 428 forbids a right turn at the next junction; when it's placed above the traffic light, the prohibition also includes a U-turn to the right.

questions.q: Who is a parking place marked with this sign reserved for?
options: Only an electric vehicle
Only a vehicle carrying a valid disabled badge, while it's being used by the disabled person
Only a vehicle with more than two passengers
Any vehicle, without restriction
questions.explain: Sign 437 reserves a parking place for a vehicle carrying a valid disabled badge, while it's being used by the disabled person to whom the badge was issued.

questions.q: Until when does a prohibition sign generally apply, if no earlier end sign is shown?
options: Forever, with no distance limit
Until the next junction
Until one kilometre from the sign
Until the end of the day
questions.explain: Most prohibition signs are valid until the next junction, unless an end-of-restriction sign, such as 421, 427 or 434, ends them sooner.

questions.q: What does the sign forbid?
options: Entry by a goods vehicle whose maximum permitted weight exceeds the number shown on the sign
Parking by a goods vehicle only
Entry by any private vehicle
Overtaking a goods vehicle
questions.explain: Sign 406 forbids entry by a goods vehicle whose maximum permitted weight, in tonnes, exceeds the number shown on the sign.

questions.q: What does the sign restrict?
options: The type of fuel permitted for use
Use of the road, lane or shoulder to only the vehicles stated on the sign, on the days and hours stated
The permitted direction of travel on the road
The driving speed on the road
questions.explain: Sign 501 permits driving on the road, lane or shoulder only to the vehicles stated on it, on the days and hours set.

questions.q: A private vehicle stops within the area marked by a taxi-stand sign, to drop off a passenger. Is this permitted?
options: Permitted only if there's no taxi at the stand
Permitted only at night
Yes, without restriction
No, any stopping by another vehicle within the area is forbidden, except to drop off passengers
questions.explain: Within a taxi stand (507), stopping or parking by any other vehicle is forbidden, except to drop off passengers.

questions.q: Next to a kerb painted red-yellow there is a sign showing a bus. Who may stop there?
options: No vehicle, not even a bus
Only a bus, and only to pick up or drop off passengers
Any vehicle, for any purpose
Only a taxi
questions.explain: Sign 511 permits stopping along a red-yellow kerb only for the type of vehicle stated on the sign above it, and only to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.q: What does a blue background on a guide sign indicate?
options: Expressway
A destination within the city
Local road
Tourist site
questions.explain: A blue background on guide signs indicates destinations on a expressway; green - non-urban, brown - tourism, white or black - local urban.

questions.q: What does the sign indicate?
options: One-way road
Educational-institutions area
Two close-spaced exits
Dead-end road
questions.explain: Sign 623 indicates that the road ahead is a dead end, with no connection to another road.

questions.q: On a road number sign, which colour indicates a expressway?
options: Green
Brown
Blue
Black
questions.explain: A expressway number appears in blue; a main road in red, a regional road in green and a local road in black.

questions.q: What is the role of the appendix symbols (S1 to S141) that mostly appear on guide signs?
options: To mark a maximum speed
To indicate a no-overtaking prohibition
To indicate a specific service or site, such as a petrol station or a hospital
To replace the guide sign itself
questions.explain: The appendix symbols are added to guide signs to indicate a specific facility, service or site, such as a petrol station, a hospital or a tourist site.

questions.q: What does this sign mark?
options: The start of a worksite on the road
An emergency stopping bay
A barrier that closes the road completely
End of the worksite
questions.explain: Sign 901 marks the start of the worksite on the road, until sign 902.

questions.q: At a worksite, an orange line is marked on the road where there used to be a permanent white line. Which line do you follow?
options: The temporary orange line
Whichever line is further from the vehicle
You may ignore both lines
The old white line, because it's the permanent one
questions.explain: A temporary sign or marking at a worksite, usually in orange, overrides the permanent sign or marking at the same place.

questions.q: A flagger at a worksite signals with their hand to stop, while the nearby traffic light shows green. How should you act?
options: Choose whatever seems safer at that moment
Sound the horn and wait for a further instruction
Stop, following the flagger's instruction
Drive according to the traffic light, because it's the permanent one
questions.explain: You must obey an authorised flagger's instruction even when it contradicts a traffic light or a sign (reg. 23).
